script.title: Why This Family Fled 160 Miles Into Siberia
script.hook_text: Found Hidden in Siberia After Decades
sentences: In 1978, a helicopter pilot spotted a cabin deep in Siberia.
It sat 160 miles from any settlement, near the Yerinat River.
Inside lived Karp Lykov, hiding with his family for decades.
Karp fled in 1936 after a Soviet patrol killed his brother.
He took his wife Akulina and two children into the taiga.
Two more children were born during their isolated life.
A few locals knew of them, but they avoided modern society.
When geologists finally found them, the Lykovs refused to leave.
For this family, the freezing wilderness was safer than civilization.
script.description:
In 1978, geologists discovered the Lykov family living in the remote Siberian taiga after fleeing Soviet repression in 1936.
Learn how this Old Believer family survived decades in deep isolation.

claims_en: In 1978, a helicopter pilot flying a geological group spotted the Lykov family's dwelling in Siberia.
The Lykov dwelling was located near the Yerinat River, 160 miles (250 km) from any settlement.
Karp Lykov lived in the Siberian cabin with his family after spending decades in partial isolation.
Karp Lykov fled his hometown in 1936 after his brother was killed by a Soviet patrol.
Karp Lykov fled into the wilderness with his wife Akulina and their two children Savin and Natalia.
Two additional children, Dmitry and Agafia, were born during the family's isolation.
Locals were in contact with the family over the years despite their partial isolation.
When geologists made contact with the Lykov family in 1978, the Lykovs decided not to leave.
